summary:
ICURUS is an AI-powered assistant designed to simplify the analysis of satellite and space observation data. We developed an agentic system that allows users to interact with complex geospatial and remote-sensing imagery through natural language queries rather than relying entirely on multiple specialized tools and manual workflows.

The platform integrates vision-language models and specialized AI models to perform tasks such as satellite image analysis, object identification, change detection, and SAR-optical data analysis. It also provides interactive visualizations, key findings, metadata, and information about the data and processing pipeline.

ICURUS addresses the challenge of making satellite data analysis more accessible, efficient, and interpretable, particularly for researchers and professionals who work with large volumes of observational data. By bringing multiple analytical capabilities into a unified interface, it reduces the complexity of exploring and interpreting satellite imagery.

The project is important because satellite observations have significant applications in environmental monitoring, disaster management, infrastructure analysis, and scientific research. ICURUS aims to bridge the gap between complex satellite data and actionable insights.
details:
Project Details – ICURUS

ICURUS is an AI-powered, agentic assistant designed to simplify the analysis and interpretation of satellite and space observation data. It allows users to interact with complex observational imagery through natural language queries, reducing the need to navigate multiple specialized tools and manually interpret large datasets.

How it works:
ICURUS uses an LLM-driven orchestration system to understand user queries, identify the appropriate analytical task, and route requests to specialized AI models. Its capabilities include satellite image analysis, object identification, change detection, and SAR-optical cross-modal analysis. The platform also provides interactive geospatial visualizations, key findings, metadata, and information about data sources and processing pipelines, helping users understand not just the results but also how they were obtained.

Benefits and intended impact:
The project aims to make satellite data analysis more accessible, efficient, and interpretable for researchers, scientists, and professionals. It can support applications such as environmental monitoring, disaster management, infrastructure assessment, and scientific research. By integrating multiple analytical capabilities into one interface, ICURUS reduces workflow fragmentation and helps users move from raw observations to meaningful insights.

Technology and tools used:

  • Programming: Python
  • Backend: FastAPI
  • AI orchestration: LangChain and LangGraph
  • Language models: LLM-based query understanding and task routing
  • Specialized AI models: EarthDial-4B-MS, Prithvi, CLOSP, and TerraFM
  • Geospatial technologies: Rasterio, GeoPandas, and PostGIS
  • Database: PostgreSQL
  • Visualization: Interactive geospatial maps and 3D globe-based visualization
  • Hardware: NVIDIA GPU-based computing infrastructure for model development and testing

Creativity and innovation:
The central innovation of ICURUS is its agentic approach to satellite data analysis. Instead of building a single model for every task, we developed a system that intelligently selects and coordinates specialized models based on the user's intent. Another important aspect is the integration of analytical results with their metadata, data provenance, and interactive visualizations. This makes the platform more than a conversational interface; it connects natural language interaction with actual domain-specific analysis.

Factors considered during development:
Our team considered model accuracy, computational requirements, GPU memory limitations, compatibility between different specialist models, scalability, response time, usability, and the reliability and interpretability of analytical results. We also focused on creating a modular architecture that could accommodate additional models and analytical capabilities as the project evolves.
